reasoning: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) returned inconclusive due to LLM API failures (HTTP 400 errors) when auditing PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO - this is a tool error, not a security finding. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully audited all text files and found them safe, with detailed analysis showing standard AUR packaging practices: PKGBUILD has no malicious top-level code, sources are fetched from official Codeberg upstream, the SKIP checksum is for a detached .asc signature (normal practice), freeipa-client.install performs legitimate IPA client system integration, and nis-domainname.service is a standard systemd unit. Report 3 (openrouter/free, advisory) corroborates these findings. No injection patterns, no execution of untrusted content, no exfiltration - all code serves the package's stated purpose of packaging FreeIPA.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from Report 1 experiencing API failures (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to audit PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. This is a tool/infrastructure failure, not a genuine security disagreement. Report 2 successfully completed the audit and found no issues.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to audit PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400)
All reports skipped ipaplatform.tar.gz (binary file) - acceptable as it's a declared source with checksum verification
No source_fetch attempted - upstream verification not performed
learnings: API failures should be clearly distinguished from security findings in verdict aggregation - a tool error causing 'inconclusive' should not trigger disagreement escalation when other models successfully complete the audit
When one model fails due to infrastructure errors and another succeeds with thorough analysis, the successful analysis should carry the verdict
Binary file skipping (tarballs, PGP keys) is appropriate when they are declared sources with checksum verification in the PKGBUILD
